compiled_state.description:
## What happened

Closing a story hit two gates that contradict each other, forcing a full extra LLM plan-review
round trip for a change that altered nothing about the plan's substance.

1. `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` refused:

   > `Error: cannot close: commit <sha> changes src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json, which the
   > recorded file_impact does not declare. Declare them with rebar set-file-impact … and retry`

2. Complying — `rebar set-file-impact` widening the list from 9 to 15 paths — then made the NEXT
   close refuse:

   > `plan-review close gate: stale-material: the plan was materially edited since review —
   > changed: file_impact (9 -> 15 paths)`

So gate 1 demands an edit that gate 2 treats as invalidating the review. The only way forward is
a fresh `review-plan` run — which is an expensive agentic LLM pass, and is exactly what is
unavailable during the outage in bug `unquieting-godsent-mammal`.

## Why the widening was legitimate, not a plan change

The added paths were files the commit genuinely touched and that no one could have declared at
plan time:

- `src/rebar/_guides/criterion-pins.json` — a GENERATED digest manifest containing no
  human-authored content. It is regenerated by
  `python -m rebar.llm.plan_review.guide_parity regenerate` whenever the criteria guide changes,
  so it is a mechanical consequence of the work, not a scope decision.
- `src/rebar/_guides/writing-a-passing-plan.md` and `tests/unit/test_guides.py` — absorbed
  mid-flight when a Gerrit code review correctly required a sibling story's file to move into
  this change (splitting one file across two stacked changes left the shipped guide misquoting
  its own coach output).

Neither alters what the plan commits to. The attestation's purpose — proving a human/agent
reviewed the intended work — is not weakened by declaring MORE of what that work actually
touched.

## Suggested direction (not a prescription)

A purely ADDITIVE `file_impact` correction, made to satisfy the completion gate's own demand,
is a candidate for not staling the attestation — or for a cheap re-attestation path that does
not re-run the agentic review (the existing `rebar sign-review` re-signs from the sidecar when
the review itself is still valid; something analogous may fit here). A REMOVAL from
`file_impact`, or an edit to the description or acceptance criteria, should keep staling as it
does today.

Whatever the fix, the two gates should not be able to demand mutually exclusive things.

## Reproduction

1. Claim a story with a recorded `file_impact`, earn its plan-review attestation.
2. Commit work that also touches a generated file the plan did not declare (e.g. regenerate
   `criterion-pins.json`).
3. `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` → refused, demands the path be declared.
4. `rebar set-file-impact <id>` adding that path.
5. `rebar transition <id> in_progress closed` → refused as `stale-material`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The completion gate's "declare these paths" remediation, when followed exactly, does not
      by itself put the ticket into `stale-material`.
- [ ] An additive-only `file_impact` correction is distinguished from a substantive plan edit,
      with the substantive cases (description, acceptance criteria, path REMOVAL) still staling
      the attestation as they do today.
- [ ] A test drives the exact five-step reproduction above and asserts the close succeeds
      without a fresh agentic `review-plan` run.
compiled_state.title: Close gate demands a file_impact edit that then stales the attestation
